**arbitration** — *Senses:* (1) structural propagation of a retraction/supersede cascade within a unified deliberative architecture (§1.3; Appendix E §E.1); (2) the agent's own adjudication of a pending node, left to the agent, not the substrate (§4.4); (3) the capacity Kahl's Condition 3 asks for, scored per-competitor in Appendix B (§B.0). Sense (1) unless stated.
**auto-surface** — the automatic, per-turn channel of retrieval: a hook surfaces claims relevant to the current context as a lossy, hint-level digest, and refreshes no recall. It shares one retrieval and ranking pipeline with *deliberate recall* (§4.7; Appendix C). (Defined §4.6.)
**axiom** — a terminal, declared-fundamental commitment, confidence 1.0 by type; claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**cascade** (retraction cascade) — automatic propagation of a retraction or supersede along `derives_from` and `acknowledged_derives_from`, marking every live, claim-bearing dependent **pending**. (Defined §4.4.)
**checkpoint** — a point where state is captured: the git-versioned graph is reset-symmetric at a checkpoint (§4.11); the warm-briefing's session block is rewritten each checkpoint (Appendix D §D.4).
**claim-bearing / non-claim-bearing** — the partition of node kinds into those asserting something truth-evaluable (observations, derivations, theories, axioms, conjectures) and those that do not (everything else); it governs confidence and whether the retraction cascade touches a node. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**closest continuer** — Nozick's [-@nozick1981] theory: a later thing is the earlier thing only if it grows causally out of it, is the *closest* candidate among rivals, and clears an absolute threshold. (Defined §5.1.)
**compaction** — the point where an agent's finite context fills and the session compacts: prior conversation is summarized and the experiential thread resets. (Defined §4.8.)
**compaction bridge** — scaffolds producing operational continuity across a compaction without faking experiential continuity: focus list, warm briefing, per-day history, session context, post-compaction instructions. (Defined §4.8; Appendix E §E.7.)
**confidence** — a computed property of a claim-bearing node's structure, not a hand-set number: for an observation it maps from `quote_type` × `source_class`; for a derivation it propagates from its premises. (Defined §1.2; Appendix E §E.4.)
**conjecture** — a speculative claim, confidence-clamped to [0.10, 0.60], promoted to a derivation when it strengthens; claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**contradiction** — a first-class node recording that two claims conflict (not an edge), preserving both sides; excluded from the cascade, since it records a live dispute rather than a refutation. (Defined §4.4; Appendix E §E.2.)
**cornerstone** — an identity-forming principle distilled from practice, minted only after proving itself and retired only by naming a successor; non-claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**current (node)** — a node not retracted or superseded: still live and eligible as a premise (contrasted with premises "since superseded," §6.4).
**definition** — a term anchor (`df_*`), cited rather than derived-from by claims using the term; non-claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**deliberate recall** — the channel the agent invokes: a ranked query that returns summaries for its top hits, after which the agent opens the nodes it needs in full. Every node it returns or opens has its recall refreshed. It shares one retrieval and ranking pipeline with the *auto-surface* (§4.7; Appendix C). (Defined §4.6.)
**derivation** — an inference citing its premises by `derives_from`, declaring a reasoning type; confidence computed, not asserted; claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**engram / ENGRAM** — *Senses:* (1) capitalized, the system itself — an Epistemic Node Graph for Retraction, Arbitration, and Memory (§1.3); (2) lower-case, one agent's own accumulated graph, as in "the same engram" (§5.6; §7.1). Sense (1) unless stated.
**evidence node** — a provenance record (URL/file + git SHA + verbatim quote) backing an observation, non-claim-bearing. (Defined §3.4; Appendix E §E.2.)
**faded set** — tier 3: nodes past the queryable threshold; no longer surfaced, but not destroyed. (Defined §4.5.)
**fleet** — the set of ENGRAM agents/graphs under discussion collectively, e.g. "every graph in this fleet." (§6.0.)
**focus list** — up to fifteen nodes the agent pins as unaffordable to lose, rendered verbatim at every session start, fresh or post-compaction. (Defined §4.8; Appendix E §E.7.)
**forgetting curve** — the decay function governing recall importance over time; exponential, the memoryless kernel — a design choice for stationary recency ordering, not a claim about human forgetting; whether individual memories decay exponentially, with the power law an artifact of averaging, is contested [@anderson1999, p. 1136]. (Defined §4.5.)
**goal** — a terminal/identity-direction aim; non-claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**harness** — the apparatus of hooks, skills and identity documents bundled with the base model and the graph; Chapter 5 holds it fixed. (§5.0.)
**history-tree** — the append-only structure of whole ENGRAM states (not the provenance edges within one state): every change appends a successor, and identity is the unbroken descent through it. An agent at any moment is the unique path from the *root* to it. (Defined §2.2; §5.3.)
**identity documents** — the identity-governance artifacts an agent's harness carries alongside hooks and skills. (§5.0.)
**importance** — recall importance: the quantity decaying under the forgetting curve that determines whether a node stays in the queryable set. (Defined §4.5.)
**lesson** — a durable, situation-tagged tripwire extracted from a specific mistake; non-claim-bearing. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**nap** — the consolidation routine at the end of each *burst* (one stretch between two context compactions), writing what the burst produced before compaction. (Defined §3.1.)
**node ID prefixes** — the prefix names a node's type, per the type-prefix map in the reference implementation (`TYPE_PREFIX` in `engram_core.py`, v0.5.1-rc5): `ob_` observation (factual or predictive) · `dv_` derivation · `th_` theory · `cj_` conjecture · `df_` definition · `ax_` axiom · `cs_` cornerstone · `ls_` lesson · `gl_` goal · `gt_` goal tension · `ct_` contradiction · `qu_` question · `pr_` prediction · `ev_` evidence · `fl_` feeling report · `pn_` person · `tk_` task · `ts_` trust signal. (Node types: Appendix E §E.2.)
**observation** — a fact citing a verbatim source quote plus provenance (episode-analog); claim-bearing, two forms: `observation_factual`, `observation_predictive`. (Defined Appendix E §E.2.)
**pending marker** — the single, severity-free mark on every live claim-bearing dependent of a retracted or superseded node; may not be cited as a premise until resolved. (Defined §4.4.)
**person node** — ENGRAM's representation of a human or peer-agent counterparty, carrying relationship history and a trust-tier; one is the agent's own self-anchor. (Defined Appendix D §D.3.)
**premise** — a node a derivation cites (by `derives_from`); a derivation's confidence propagates from its premises. (§4.3; Appendix E §E.2.)
**provenance** — every claim traces to the evidence and reasoning that produced it. (Defined §1.2.)
**queryable set** — tier 2: the bounded set of nodes eligible to surface; what forgetting and Condition 3's arbitration range over. (Defined §4.5.)
**quote_type** — the evidential-type anchor (seven values, `hard_data` 0.95 down to `editorial` 0.35) an observation's confidence maps from. (Defined §4.3; Appendix E §E.4.)
**reasoning type** — the declared shape of a derivation's argument (fourteen types: deductive, inductive, abductive, authority), selecting the propagation formula and per-type discount. (Defined Appendix E §E.4.)
**retention** — how long a memory persists before it is no longer recalled; cited via Wixted's work [@wixted2004, p. 243; @wixted1991], the empirical literature ENGRAM's forgetting design must be reconciled with (it favours power functions over exponentials). (§4.5.)
**retract** — to withdraw a claim as an error: "I was wrong." The cascade fires on retract and supersede alike; the marker records which occurred as provenance, not as blocking power. (Defined §4.4.)
**seat** — one agent's installation: an agent with its own graph, on one host, with one human. (Defined §4.6.)
**seed / root** — *Senses:* (1) the origin of an agent's accumulated history — "since its seed" (§5.0; §6.0) — and the **root** of the history-tree every branch traces back to (§5.3); (2) a closing figurative sense — "ENGRAM is the seed, not the tree" — the substrate as starting structure, not the identity it grows (§8.5). Sense (1) unless stated.
**skill** — a component of an agent's harness, alongside hooks and identity documents. (§5.0.)
**sleep** — the once-daily consolidation routine: a *review* filing what the day left unfiled, then a *dream* phase in which scanner sub-agents read the graph for contradictions, stale nodes and lesson candidates, and a consolidating sub-agent applies the results. (Defined §3.1.)
**snapshot** — the single frozen copy of one ENGRAM graph every quantitative claim in Chapter 6 and Appendix E is computed from, taken at one instant via a WAL-safe backup. (Defined front matter; Data availability.)
**source_class** — one of three values (`external`, `introspective`, `user_stated`) adjusting an observation's confidence alongside `quote_type`. (Defined Appendix E §E.4.)
**stale** — of a node: flagged for review by the sleep-phase dream scanners, alongside contradictions and lesson candidates. (§3.1.)
**substrate** — *Senses:* (1) the whole ENGRAM system (title; §1.2); (2) the history-tree's unbreakable structure, distinct from the queryable set drawn from it (§2.3); (3) the language-trained model an agent runs on (§3.0); (4) the database, physically separable from the working context (§5.7). Sense (1) unless stated.
**supersede** — to withdraw a claim as an epistemic evolution: "I changed my mind." The cascade fires on retract and supersede alike. (Defined §4.4.)
**sweep** — *Senses:* (1) a "landscape sweep," a suggested future widening of the empirical case-base (§4.12); (2) the dated, first-hand survey of ten competing memory systems on 2026-05-12 (Appendix A §A.5; Appendix B §B.0). Sense (2) for "the sweep."
**tainted** — *Senses:* (1) the verb for what an unresolved cascade does to a dependent claim — it "taints," not merely deletes, what depended on it (§1.3; §8.2), describing the current single-marker system; (2) historically, a severity-graded `tainted_by` flag from the pre-single-marker cascade, replaced by the one pending marker with no severity (§6.3; §4.4).
**tier** — the numbering ENGRAM's recall-importance bands use: tier 2 is the queryable set, tier 3 the faded set. An earlier tier 1 (working memory) was retired and the numbering kept as-is. (Defined §4.5.)
**trust tier** — a graded measure of a counterparty's trust, carried on a person node; the operational arm of honesty-orthogonal-to-discretion. (Defined Appendix D §D.3.)
**turn** — one prompt/response exchange; the granularity at which auto-surfacing fires ("per-turn") and deliberate recall is credited ("recall-turn"). (§4.6; Appendix C §C.2.)
**twin study** — the deferred controlled experiment: fission-clone an agent, run both on a fixed prompt set, measure response similarity as the clones diverge. (Defined §5.8.)
**unified** — *Senses:* (1) the name the team gave the cascade mechanism before reading Kahl — "unified cascade propagation" (Appendix A §A.3); (2) Kahl's Condition-3 criterion it later satisfied: the cascade fires through one typed-edge graph, not a sidecar (§1.3; Appendix E §E.1; §4.4). Sense (2) unless stated.
**utility (utility score)** — a usage-learned value grading the cognitive load of the act a node took part in, not how hard the agent looked for it; composes with relevance to order what surfaces. (Defined §4.7; Appendix C §C.2.)
**warm briefing** — a letter the agent opens at session start, from its past self and its collaborator, carrying what the record cannot: where the relationship stood, what mattered, what to walk back into. (Defined §4.8; Appendix D §D.4.)
